_readme: The Perspective Cards deck. Every card is a role, a way of thinking or a set of conditions, never a named person (BRIEF 8.6 and section 2.1). 'book' marks a card that comes from the book (Ch9 Shoe Swapper 'inexpert witnesses' and the gang of five children; Ch4 'Different Strokes'); every other card and every 'ask' line is ours. Use US English.

groups.label: Fresh eyes
groups.about: People who know little about your problem and are not held back by what has been tried.

groups.label: People with a stake
groups.about: People who care about the outcome, each for a different reason.

groups.label: Ways of thinking
groups.about: Different habits of mind: quick, thorough, careful, bold.

groups.label: Different conditions
groups.about: The same problem under different limits of time, money and scale.

cards.name: A five-year-old child
cards.ask: What is the simplest way to say the problem, and what would they ask why about?

cards.name: A passenger in a taxi
cards.ask: What would they notice from the back seat that the driver no longer sees?

cards.name: A roofer
cards.ask: What would they check first, and what would they fix with what is already on hand?

cards.name: A novelist
cards.ask: What is the story here, and where does the plot go wrong?

cards.name: A touring musician
cards.ask: What would they leave behind to travel light, and what could not be left?

cards.name: A sushi chef
cards.ask: What would they strip away until only the essential is left?

cards.name: A jockey
cards.ask: Where is the extra weight, and when is the moment to make a move?

cards.name: Someone from a different department
cards.ask: What do they know about this that your team does not?

cards.name: Someone on their first day
cards.ask: What is confusing here that everyone else has stopped noticing?

cards.name: A visitor who has never heard of your field
cards.ask: What would you have to explain in one sentence, and what question would they ask next?

cards.name: A teacher of seven-year-olds
cards.ask: How would they turn this into something a class could understand and try?

cards.name: A librarian
cards.ask: How would they organize this so that anyone could find what they need?

cards.name: A farmer
cards.ask: What has to be planted now so that it is ready in a season?

cards.name: A nurse on a night shift
cards.ask: What would they do with too little time and too many demands?

cards.name: A tourist in your town
cards.ask: What would they find hard to work out, and what would delight them?

cards.name: A mayor
cards.ask: What does this cost the city, in time and in business, and who will complain?
cards.book: Ch4 The Answer Is in the Question

cards.name: A police chief
cards.ask: Where does this create accidents or a drain on people and resources?
cards.book: Ch4 The Answer Is in the Question

cards.name: An environmentalist
cards.ask: What does this do to the air, the water and the ground?
cards.book: Ch4 The Answer Is in the Question

cards.name: A regular commuter
cards.ask: How much of their day does this take, and how stressful is it?
cards.book: Ch4 The Answer Is in the Question

cards.name: A first-time customer
cards.ask: What would make them trust you in the first minute?

cards.name: A customer of ten years
cards.ask: What would make them leave, and what keeps them?

cards.name: A supplier
cards.ask: What would they need from you to do their best work?

cards.name: The person who has to approve the budget
cards.ask: What is the first thing they will ask, and what would make them say yes?

cards.name: Someone who has to maintain it in five years
cards.ask: What will break, and what will they wish you had written down?

cards.name: Your fiercest competitor
cards.ask: How would they respond, and what would they copy?

cards.name: A safety inspector
cards.ask: What could go wrong, and how would you show that it will not?

cards.name: A neighbor who lives next door
cards.ask: What would they hear, see and smell, and what would they say about it?

cards.name: Someone who has put money in
cards.ask: How does this pay back, and what would worry them?

cards.name: A customer who cannot use it the usual way
cards.ask: What would they need to be changed, and who else would it help?

cards.name: The peacemaker
cards.ask: Which idea takes the feelings of the most people into account?
cards.book: Ch9 Shoe Swapper (the gang of five)

cards.name: The wide thinker
cards.ask: What other areas is this problem linked to, and what do they teach?
cards.book: Ch9 Shoe Swapper (the gang of five)

cards.name: The quick decider
cards.ask: What is the first solution that could be tried right now?
cards.book: Ch9 Shoe Swapper (the gang of five)

cards.name: The thorough explorer
cards.ask: Which avenues have not been explored yet, and what is down each?
cards.book: Ch9 Shoe Swapper (the gang of five)

cards.name: The pioneer
cards.ask: What has nobody tried, and why does that make it interesting?
cards.book: Ch9 Shoe Swapper (the gang of five)

cards.name: The builder
cards.ask: What could you make this afternoon to test the idea?

cards.name: The storyteller
cards.ask: How would you tell this so that people remember it?

cards.name: The skeptic
cards.ask: What would have to be true for this to work, and how would you check?

cards.name: The saver
cards.ask: What is the cheapest version that still does the job?

cards.name: The planner
cards.ask: What has to happen first, second and third?

cards.name: Someone with no money
cards.ask: What would you do if you could not buy a solution?

cards.name: Someone with unlimited money
cards.ask: What would you do if cost did not matter, and what is the cheap version of that?

cards.name: Someone with one hour
cards.ask: What can be done in an hour, and what comes of it?

cards.name: Someone with ten years
cards.ask: What would you start now that only pays off later?

cards.name: Someone living in the year 2075
cards.ask: What will they find strange about how we do this today?

cards.name: Yourself in five years
cards.ask: What will you wish you had done now?

cards.name: Someone who has one sentence
cards.ask: What is the one sentence, and what does it leave out?

cards.name: A motor-racing pit crew
cards.ask: How would they do it in seconds, with everyone knowing their part?

cards.name: A touring band's road crew
cards.ask: How would they pack it, move it and set it up again tomorrow night?

cards.name: An emergency room team
cards.ask: How would they decide what comes first when everything is urgent?

cards.name: A film crew on location
cards.ask: How would they make it work with what is there and a deadline?

cards.name: An expedition leader
cards.ask: What must be carried, and what can be left behind?

cards.name: A market stall owner
cards.ask: How would they win the next passer-by in ten seconds?

cards.name: A museum curator
cards.ask: What would you put on display, and what would you keep in storage?

cards.name: Someone with only paper and pens
cards.ask: How would you solve it with no technology at all?

cards.name: Someone who has to make it fun
cards.ask: What would change if people looked forward to it?
